chain.label: Dense freezing fog / night low IFR conditions at AUS
chain.trigger: Night instrument meteorological conditions prevailed at the time of the incident; visibility 1/4 mile; freezing fog; vertical visibility 200 ft agl; temperature -1C

chain.label: No surface detection equipment at AUS tower and no flight deck runway-conflict alerting required by FAA
chain.trigger: the AUS air traffic control tower (ATCT) did not have surface detection equipment to aid the controller in monitoring ground traffic

chain.label: ATCT had conducted no low-visibility operations or SMGCS training for 2 years; controller not current in low-visibility work
chain.trigger: the tower had not conducted training on low-visibility operations during the 2 years before the incident

chain.label: Controller's expectation bias that a SWA airplane calling ready is already at the hold-short line and will depart immediately
chain.trigger: when they [SWA pilots] call ready...they're actually holding short and they're ready. You give them the traffic and they go

chain.label: Controller did not determine or request the SWA airplane's position before issuing takeoff clearance; airplane was 550 ft from the hold-short line
chain.trigger: the controller did not verify the SWA airplane's position on the taxiway when the flight crew requested takeoff clearance and instead assumed that the SWA airplane was already at the hold-short line

caused_by.evidence: The controller was unable to see the SWA airplane on the taxiway and runway because of dense fog

the AUS ATCT did not have any surface detection equipment, which impeded the controller's ability to properly separate the SWA and FedEx airplanes given the lack of visual references outside the tower
The controller's assumption about the SWA airplane's position on the taxiway was likely due to expectation bias
the AUS ATCT had not adequately prepared the controller for the low-visibility conditions on the morning of the incident

chain.label: Controller cleared SWA for takeoff assuming it would depart before the FedEx arrival, and did not later cancel the clearance or send FedEx around
chain.trigger: the local controller's incorrect assumption that the SWA airplane would depart from the runway before the FedEx airplane arrived on the same runway, which resulted in a loss of separation between both airplanes

caused_by.evidence: because he thought that the SWA airplane was already at the hold-short line, the controller was not able to predict the loss of separation that would later occur
his expectation bias regarding the SWA airplane's departure
the ATCT's lack of training (before the incident) on low-visibility operations

chain.label: SWA crew stopped 19 seconds on the runway for a required engine run-up without telling the controller they needed extra time, despite known traffic on short final
chain.trigger: they did not inform the controller of their intention to perform an engine run-up once the airplane entered the active runway... the SWA airplane was stopped on the runway for 19 seconds

caused_by.evidence: performed a static engine run-up due to freezing fog conditions
At 0638:58, the controller cleared the SWA airplane for takeoff from runway 18L... and advised that a FedEx Boeing 767 airplane was on a 3-mile final approach

chain.label: Runway incursion: SWA airplane still on runway 18L as the FedEx airplane crossed the threshold; separation fell to 150-170 ft
chain.trigger: the 2-mile required separation between the airplanes was not maintained... At their closest point, the airplanes were separated by 150 to 170 ft

caused_by.evidence: the controller's incorrect assumption that the SWA airplane would depart before the FedEx airplane would arrive set up a hazardous situation that could have resulted in an accident
During the engine run-up, the SWA airplane was stopped on the runway for 19 seconds, which further decreased the separation between the departing SWA airplane and the approaching FedEx airplane
The FedEx captain's postincident statement indicated that the visibility was 'zero' at that point

chain.label: FedEx first officer saw the SWA airplane and called go-around; captain flew the missed approach and SWA shallowed its climb, avoiding collision with no damage or injury
chain.trigger: The flight crew of the FedEx airplane executed a missed approach to avoid a collision... The 128 occupants aboard the SWA airplane and the 3 occupants aboard the FedEx airplane were not injured, and neither airplane sustained any damage

caused_by.evidence: when the FedEx airplane was at an altitude of about 150 ft agl, he saw... the 'left white position light' of the SWA airplane followed by the airplane's 'silhouette'
